questions.q: According to Döbereiner's law of triads, what is seen in Li (7), Na (23), K (39)?
options: The middle element's mass equals the average of the other two
Each mass is double the previous one
questions.explain: (7 + 39)/2 = 23, which is the mass of Na.

questions.q: In Newlands' law of octaves, which is the eighth element from Li?
questions.explain: Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, then Na is the eighth, and Na resembles Li.

questions.q: On what basis did Mendeleev arrange the elements?
options: Increasing atomic mass and similarity of properties
questions.explain: He arranged by rising mass and broke the order in places to keep similar properties together.

questions.q: Mendeleev's 'eka-aluminium' was later discovered as which element?
questions.explain: Eka-aluminium (mass 68, low melting point) = gallium (mass ≈ 70, m.p. 302.93 K). Germanium is eka-silicon.

questions.q: What is the basis of the modern periodic law?
questions.explain: Moseley's X-ray work showed √ν varies linearly with Z.

questions.q: Why does argon (Z = 18, mass 39.95) come before potassium (Z = 19, mass 39.10)?
options: Because the order is by mass
Because the order follows atomic number and fits the properties
questions.explain: The Z order is the true one; by mass Ar and K would fall in the wrong groups.

questions.q: How many elements are there in the sixth period of the long-form table?
What is the IUPAC temporary name and symbol of the element with Z = 105?
questions.explain: 1, 0, 5 → un, nil, pent → Unnilpentium; symbol U + n + p = Unp.

questions.q: What is the temporary symbol of the element with Z = 120?
questions.explain: 1, 2, 0 → un, bi, nil → Unbinilium → Ubn.

questions.q: An element has outer configuration ns²np⁴ with n = 3. Which element is it and in which group?
questions.explain: Period 3; p-block; group = 10 + 2 + 4 = 16; 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁴ is sulphur.

questions.q: Fe (Z = 26) is [Ar]3d⁶4s². Which block and group is it?
questions.explain: (n−1)d + ns = 6 + 2 = 8; a d-block element of period 4.

questions.q: Why is helium (1s²) placed in group 18?
options: Its shell is full, so it is unreactive like the other noble gases
questions.explain: 1s² is a complete shell and its properties match the noble gases.

questions.q: Why does atomic radius decrease from left to right across a period?
options: Nuclear charge rises while electrons enter the same shell
questions.explain: A higher charge pulls the electrons in, with little change in shielding.

questions.q: Among O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺ and Mg²⁺, which has the smallest radius?
questions.explain: All have 10 electrons; Mg has the largest nuclear charge (+12).

questions.q: Why is the first ionisation enthalpy of Be (899) higher than that of B (801)?
options: B's electron is in 2p, which feels the nucleus less than 2s
Be has a smaller nuclear charge
questions.explain: A 2s electron penetrates closer to the nucleus, so it is harder to remove.

questions.q: The successive ionisation enthalpies of Mg are 738, 1451, 7733 kJ mol⁻¹. What can be concluded?
options: Mg has 2 valence electrons (big jump at the third)
questions.explain: After two electrons, the next comes from a stable inner shell, hence the big jump.

questions.q: Among P, S, Cl and F, which has the most negative electron gain enthalpy?
questions.explain: Cl: −349, F: −328 kJ mol⁻¹. F's small 2p subshell has more repulsion.

questions.q: Which element has the highest electronegativity on Pauling's scale?
questions.explain: F = 4.0 (the highest), O = 3.5, Cl = 3.0, N = 3.0.

questions.q: What kind of oxide is Al₂O₃?
questions.explain: It reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.q: Which pair shows a diagonal relationship?
questions.explain: Li (group 1, period 2) and Mg (group 2, period 3) have similar properties.
